_comment: STAGE-D per-batch coverage registry -- batch 'artifacts' (D27, Tier-2 frontend cluster)
(docs/twin_validation/wave2_6_unit_test_contract.md SS12.3/12.4; full-coverage program;
work-list docs/twin_validation/l3_release_package_unit_inventory.md D27).
Run via tests/harness/gate.py <this file> (L0+L1; calls tests/harness/coverage_audit.py) and
tests/harness/mutation.py <this file> (L2).
MODULE: frontend/artifacts.py -- the frontend's on-disk artifact layer. It imports numpy +
qec_twin.hardware.b8_io + stdlib json/hashlib/pathlib, and imports NEITHER torch NOR quimb, so
EVERY public unit is CPU-PURE and IN-SCOPE for full L0+L1+L2 -- out_of_scope is therefore {} (the
AST reconcile refuses any gpu_bound claim on a torch-less module -> expect ZERO out_of_scope).
SEVEN public units (AST reconcile _public_units_in_module: top-level public defs + every public
method of a top-level class). ArtifactPaths is a frozen dataclass with NO methods and NO
__post_init__ (only field annotations), so it contributes NO units; the seven units are the seven
module-level functions:
* artifact_paths          -- str|Path out_dir -> ArtifactPaths (16 root/<name> fields).
* write_b8                -- pack unpacked [shots,bits] bool -> Stim .b8 (two raising guards).
* write_b8_optional       -- write .b8 when width>0 else unlink stale + return None.
* write_json              -- json.dumps(_jsonable(payload), indent=2, sort_keys=True)+'\n'.
* clear_known_artifacts   -- unlink every known file field (skips out_dir).
* file_sha256             -- None-safe / missing-safe chunked sha256 of a file -> 64-hex.
* record_summary          -- JSON-safe counts/marginals/any-rates of det/obs bool records.
The private helper _jsonable (leading `_`) is NOT a public unit -- the coverage audit does not
score it -- but it IS mutated by mutmut and is exercised + pinned end-to-end through write_json
(all six type arms: ndarray/np.generic/Path/dict-recurse/list/tuple/passthrough).
L2 DISCIPLINE (100% coverage != discrimination).
* artifact_paths: EVERY one of the 16 fields is pinned to the EXACT root/<name> against an
INDEPENDENT filename table (reconstructed literally, NOT from the module's own expressions) --
a mutated filename string-literal shifts the pinned path -> `==` fails. A str out_dir input
still yields Path-typed fields (kills a removed Path(out_dir) coercion; a str root would fail
`root / name`). Both str + Path input routes exercised.
* write_b8 / write_b8_optional: the written FILE BYTES are pinned vs an INDEPENDENT
np.packbits(...,bitorder='little') recompute of the b8 wire format (NOT via b8_io). Both
raising guards (ndim!=2 shape-carrying message; zero-bit-width message) are tripped through
the PUBLIC entry with the EXACT message via assert_raises_exact. A WIDTH-1 write (shape[1]==1)
kills a `0`->`1` boundary mutant on `shape[1] <= 0` / `shape[1] == 0` (a `<=1`/`==1` mutant
would spuriously raise / skip). write_b8_optional's zero-width SKIP branch is tripped BOTH
when a stale file EXISTS (removed -> None) AND when the path is ABSENT (no raise -> None,
killing `missing_ok=True`->False).
* write_json + _jsonable: ONE payload pins the EXACT serialized text -- indent=2, sort_keys=True
(insertion order b,a != sorted a,b so the sort is load-bearing), trailing '\n' -- so an
indent/sort_keys/`+ "\n"` mutant changes the string. A SECOND payload drives all six _jsonable
arms pinned vs an INDEPENDENT native structure; an np.int64 buried inside the TUPLE makes the
tuple arm load-bearing (dropping the tuple case -> json.dumps chokes on the raw np scalar ->
raise). A str path input still returns a Path.
* clear_known_artifacts: writes all 15 file artifacts, clears, asserts each is GONE yet the
out_dir DIRECTORY survives -- an `and`->`or` / `!=`->`==` / `"out_dir"` string mutant would
unlink() the directory -> IsADirectoryError (the call raises -> killed); a mutant that never
unlinks leaves the files -> the gone-assertions fire. A SECOND clear on the now-missing files
is a no-op (kills `missing_ok=True`->False).
* file_sha256: pinned == an INDEPENDENT hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()) digest (64 lowercase
hex; whole-file, independent of the module's chunked loop). The None arm (-> None) and the
missing-file arm (-> None) are each tripped through the public entry; a str path input still
hashes (kills a removed Path(path) coercion). NB: the chunk SIZE (1024*1024) is invariant to
the sha256 digest, so numeric mutations of the chunk size are mechanical EQUIVALENTS (a
correctly-rounded per-chunk hash is identical for any positive chunk size).
* record_summary: the EXACT summary dict is pinned vs a from-scratch INDEPENDENT recompute over
a fixture whose four counts (shots 5, detectors 3, observables 2) and two any-rates (0.6 vs
0.4) are ALL DISTINCT (an axis/index/shape swap is caught), value TYPES pinned (int/list/
float), plus the all-empty arc (ndim!=2 -> 0; size==0 -> [] / 0.0; taken via empty 1D inputs
BEFORE any(axis=1) is reached) and a discriminating wrong-array.
REACHABILITY (the D13/D18/D19 default-arg / guard-route lesson -- PROBED through the PUBLIC entry
points, never asserted). Every raising guard is tripped through the real public function with a
reaching input (1D/3D array for ndim!=2; width-0 array for the zero-bit guard; explicit None and
a real absent path for file_sha256; a stale-then-missing file for write_b8_optional's skip). The
record_summary `else 0` (num_detectors/observables) and `else []`/`else 0.0` (marginals/rates)
arcs are reached with EMPTY 1D inputs: size is falsy, so the code never reaches the any(axis=1)
call that a non-empty 1D array would crash on. In clear_known_artifacts every field's value is a
Path, so `isinstance(value, Path)` is always True and its False arc is structurally unreachable
via a valid ArtifactPaths -- the `and`'s second operand (field.name != 'out_dir') supplies BOTH
the True arc (15 file fields -> unlink) and the False arc (out_dir -> skip), so the `if` line's
two arcs are both covered.
NO exemptions + NO out_of_scope: every SCORED unit is CPU-pure and every branch of its OWN AST
body is REACHABLE through a public entry point.
